topics.topic: Authoritative lifecycle field for access creation when Registry fields disagree
questions: For an inconsistent validation answer with `status='archived'` and `is_active=true`, must grant or assignment creation be refused or admitted?
When Registry returns `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, and `is_active=true`, must creation be admitted or refused?
When exists, is_active, and status disagree, which field determines whether a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant may be created?

quotes:
no new viewer grant, staff assignment
or producer grant is created for an archived project, because each creation
validates that the Registry project is active

an answer with
`is_active = true` admits the creation whatever its `status` says.
judgement.divergence: With `status = archived` and `is_active = true`, one implementation refuses access creation while another stores it; the administrator and newly granted principal notice.
judgement.why: State 0 defines archival by Registry status, while State 2 explicitly admits access creation solely from a true `is_active` value even when status says archived.

bases.passage:
no new viewer grant, staff assignment
or producer grant is created for an archived project, because each creation
validates that the Registry project is active

an answer with
`is_active = true` admits the creation whatever its `status` says.
bases.rests_on:
Portal mutation policy uses only `is_active` for the grant and assignment
operations of access management and only `status` (`active` or not) in the
project guard of State 2 A4/A5; archived context remains readable.

unsupported_sides:
no new viewer grant, staff assignment
or producer grant is created for an archived project, because each creation
validates that the Registry project is active

witness.initial: An active administrator has `portal.access.manage`; Registry validation for project P returns `exists = true`, `status = archived`, and `is_active = true`.
events: The administrator requests creation of a viewer grant for P.
outcomes: R0-24 refuses the grant because Registry reports P archived.
A6 admits and stores the grant because `is_active` is true regardless of `status`.
basis:
Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and
project grants, staff accounts and assignments, service principals, their
credentials and producer grants all require the access-management capability,
which only administrators hold (R2).

The gateway returns a
decoded validation answer as it is and raises no failure for it; it does not
check that `exists`, `is_active` and `status` agree, and each caller trusts
only the field A5 names for it.

provenance.quote: no new viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant is created for an archived project, because each creation valida

Portal mutation policy uses only is_active for the grant and assignment operations of access management and only status

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about expense authorization preceding recognition, money, allocation, and replay validation.

precedent.topic: Ordering of expense content validation and project-access authorization
quotes:
1. The route authorizes with
   `capability:authorization_guard.authorize_staff_project_mutation`.
2. `capability:expense_intake.create_expense_from_recognition` accepts only a
   confirmed complete result of a supported contract version, validates the
   total and the explicit allocations — every section of the project
   (`capability:budget_management.validate_project_section`), positive amounts,
   exact sum, no proportional split — then in one transaction looks up the
   `recognized_document_id`: absent — insert the expense, its allocations and
   one client-visible document and append `expense.create`; same fingerprint —
   return the existing expense as replay; different — conflict.
precedent.why: The later flow orders staff project authorization before recognition, item, money, allocation, and replay validation.

precedent.topic: ProjectOverview shape and validation after a Registry context-read failure
quotes:
`ProjectOverview`: six pairs — project, budget, expenses, progress, payments,
photos — each a `ViewAvailability` and a value present only when available.

A21 (derived at read time, nothing persisted), A27 and Factory
`d2c4511ea119`: a part whose builder answers `ScopedNotFoundError` is
`not_configured`, a persistence or Registry failure `temporarily_unavailable`;
no zero is fabricated; viewer photos are client-visible only.
precedent.why: State 5 defines ProjectOverview as six availability/value pairs and converts a Registry context failure into temporary unavailability.

topics.topic: Provisioning, versioning, and isolation of the vulnerability audit tool
questions: Is the scanner present in the shipped image, installed temporarily into it, or run from a separate image/environment against the shipped environment?
How is the mandated audit command made available without silently changing the installed and audited dependency set?
How is the audit tool installed and versioned, and is it present in the final runtime image or only in a reproducible audit stage that inspects the final environment?

quotes:
The check is reproducible and is one command: `pip-audit --local`, run
   inside the built image against what is installed there, querying the
   PyPI advisory database (OSV) at the time of the deploy; its result alone
   decides.

Only the four
   direct packages are pinned; pip resolves their own dependencies when the
   image is built, so those versions may differ between deploys, and the
   check audits the set resolved for the deploy at hand.
judgement.why: Provisioning and isolating a deployment-time scanner is an operational implementation note owned by State 7, not a State 2 behavioral rule.

topics.topic: Transport-guard ordering and viewer-entry rate-limit accounting
questions: What is the exact precedence among host validation, request-size validation, rate limiting, origin validation, request decoding and authentication?
What is the exact order of trusted-host, size, origin, request decoding, and viewer-entry rate-limit checks?
At what exact point relative to body-size enforcement, JSON parsing, and request-model validation is a viewer-entry attempt counted?

quotes:
For every request, in order: a request id with no identity in it; 400 for an
untrusted host; CORS preflight 204 for a listed origin and 403 for another;
403 for a viewer logout from another origin than the public one; 413 for a
body over `max_request_body_bytes`; 429 for viewer entries over the
monotonic-clock rate limit, before any credential is parsed; then the route,
called once.
judgement.why: State 5 gives the complete transport-guard order; within-size malformed JSON reaches route decoding only after viewer-entry rate-limit accounting.

topics.topic: Access-management operations covered by the is_active rule
questions: Does the is_active rule apply only to creation, or also to revocation and any other grant/assignment operation?

quotes:
revoking a viewer grant, a staff assignment or a producer grant is access
  management: it requires a valid administrator session, an active
  principal and `portal.access.manage`, and consults neither project access
  nor the Registry, so it succeeds for an archived project and during a
  Registry outage (R0-24);
judgement.why: The explicit revocation exception says revocation never consults Registry, so the `is_active` rule applies to creation rather than revocation.

precedent.topic: Check order for creating grants and staff assignments
quotes:
1. Every operation starts with
   `capability:authorization_guard.authorize_access_management`, completed
   before its own transaction opens.

5. `capability:staff_identity.assign_staff_project` validates the project with
   `capability:registry_gateway.validate_project_reference` before its
   transaction — unknown is not found, not active is refused as archived —
   refuses a duplicate active assignment and appends `staff_assignment.create`.

5. `capability:viewer_access.grant_viewer_project` requires the project known
   and active (`capability:registry_gateway.validate_project_reference`,
   before the transaction), an active viewer and no active grant for the pair,
   and appends `grant.create`.
precedent.why: The later flows require access-management authorization first, Registry validation before the write transaction, and target and duplicate checks within the owning grant or assignment operation.

precedent.topic: Concrete and concealed outcomes for project-access guard failures
quotes:
`AuthenticationRejected` for an unknown, revoked or expired session or a
non-active account; `ScopedNotFoundError` for an operator without an active
assignment or a project the Registry does not know; `AuthorizationRejected`
for a role outside the scope rule or without the capability;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
precedent.why: State 5 maps staff and viewer guard failures to their exact concealed exception classes.

judgement.why: State 4 makes readiness depend only on opening and rolling back a portal-store transaction, not on Registry or other external services.

topics.topic: Validity and normalization of EUR snapshot section amounts
questions: What exact predicate and normalization, if any, define a valid snapshot section amount?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about excess fractional precision and ROUND_HALF_UP normalization of accepted money.

precedent.topic: Handling monetary values with excess fractional precision
quotes: The amount quantized to two digits, ROUND_HALF_UP.
precedent.why: State 5 specifies that accepted boundary money is quantized to two digits using ROUND_HALF_UP.

topics.topic: Whether all advisories or only applicable vulnerabilities block deployment
questions: Does every reported advisory block deployment, or only vulnerabilities judged to affect the portal?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about whether every reported advisory blocks deployment without an applicability assessment.

quotes:
Every advisory it
reports for any resolved package blocks the deploy; "affects the portal"
is not judged case by case, so an advisory for an unused optional feature
blocks too.
precedent.why: The normative rule explicitly requires every reported advisory to block without a portal-relevance assessment.
